title: Gummi round4: enemy shots, collision and Drain ownership
status: Source/tests/catalog/research frozen; slots360/361 implemented;208 own synthetic checks pass. Root independently reviewed source and found no blocker. Common integration remains root-owned; no live tests.
original_path: E:\SteamLibrary\steamapps\common\KINGDOM HEARTS -HD 1.5+2.5 ReMIX-\KINGDOM HEARTS II FINAL MIX.exe

evidence_summary.note: Initial75 complete bodies were captured before a local health-readiness mismatch. Root then reopened the same annotated IDB with real auto_wait and captured8 supplemental owner/collision functions. All actual line counts and start addresses were checked independently. claims.Finding: Allocates and initializes 768 ENEMY_SHOT records (176 bytes each), a count header of 768, 768 main sprite records and 128 impact sprite records. Each object receives the ENEMY_SHOT vtable and its permanent sprite index; inactive flags, impact=-1 and attraction owner=0 are initialized.
claims.Limitations: Allocation/effect creation assumes working native resources. This is not a proposed trainer construction entrypoint. Static analysis; no live execution in this round.

claims.Finding: Spawns only projectile type33 into the first inactive member of the fixed 768-entry pool. It clears transient impact/attraction fields, calls the inherited initializer, sets flags0x28 and records a spatial source index. A full pool returns0.
claims.Limitations: The returned pointer is borrowed from the pool and must not survive subsystem teardown. Static analysis; no live execution in this round.

claims.Finding: The inherited projectile initializer copies the 48-byte attack descriptor, initializes position/direction/speed/lifetime, sets flags0x1100 and optionally coordinate-space bit2. It does not set individually allocated flag1.
claims.Limitations: Generic initializer semantics alone do not establish the type or ownership of arbitrary caller objects. Static analysis; no live execution in this round.

claims.Finding: Enumerates active ENEMY_SHOT entries using flag0x100 and stride176, with null as the initial cursor and a maximum index of767.
claims.Limitations: Caller-supplied nonnull cursor is assumed to belong to the current pool. A trainer should bound its own scan rather than pass stale cursors. Static analysis; no live execution in this round.

claims.Finding: Clears all active entries of exactly the ENEMY_SHOT pool by calling active predicate23E020 then deactivation23DAC0 for each of768 records. The relevant return value is not a success status.
claims.Limitations: This excludes laser and other projectile families and does not prevent future enemy firing. Static analysis; no live execution in this round.

claims.Finding: Returns whether projectile flags+128 contain active bit0x100.
claims.Limitations: It validates no pointer, object type or lifetime. Static analysis; no live execution in this round.

claims.Finding: Clears active bit0x100, invokes virtual cleanup slot+48, and only if ownership flag1 is set invokes the deleting destructor with argument1.
claims.Limitations: A trainer must reject pooled objects with flag1 or changed vtables/callbacks before using the bulk clear. Static analysis; no live execution in this round.

claims.Finding: ENEMY_SHOT virtual cleanup writes zero only to DWORD(mainSpriteBuffer + 16*spriteIndex + 12), using signed index+152. It does not award score, drop items, allocate or free memory.
claims.Limitations: Bounds and current buffer ownership are caller invariants. Impact sprites are not directly cleared here. Static analysis; no live execution in this round.

claims.Finding: The subsystem frame update selects visibility for main/impact effects from active entries and impact index, then dispatches23DB00 for each active projectile and deactivates entries returningfalse.
claims.Limitations: This is a live update loop, not a safe general trainer call because it advances collision and movement. Static analysis; no live execution in this round.

claims.Finding: Destroys and zeros both effect handles, frees main/impact sprite buffers, and invokes the pool vector destructor. Pool/buffer globals themselves are left nonzero.
claims.Limitations: A nonnull AF8288/AF8278 value is insufficient proof of a live subsystem. Static analysis; no live execution in this round.

claims.Finding: ENEMY_SHOT deleting destructor can traverse a vector using the count immediately before the first element and free its header. The per-entry clear path avoids this when flag1 is absent.
claims.Limitations: Calling this on the live pool would destroy engine-owned storage. Static analysis; no live execution in this round.

claims.Finding: The base MISSILE constructor initializes position vectors, an attack descriptor and flags0 before ENEMY_SHOT construction replaces its vtable.
claims.Limitations: Constructor output is incomplete without the subtype and subsystem initialization. Static analysis; no live execution in this round.

claims.Finding: Projectile update performs sprite initialization/update, spatial registration, collision callbacks, world collision, previous-position capture and virtual movement in that order. Collision precedes the movement callback that consumes attraction.
claims.Limitations: The full generic callback family is wider than the proposed ENEMY_SHOT clear call. Static analysis; no live execution in this round.

claims.Finding: Integrates projectile position and acceleration using native timing, decreases remaining lifetime, computes fade below10ticks, and terminates when time<0 or flag0x200. Flag0x20 can hold lifetime at10 until a distance limit is crossed.
claims.Limitations: Ticks are native timing units, not established milliseconds. This does not justify a universal projectile-speed override. Static analysis; no live execution in this round.

claims.Finding: Stores a GUMISHIP attraction target in ENEMY_SHOT+160 without retaining or validating its owner.
claims.Limitations: It is a one-frame borrowed pointer, not an ownership or reference-count operation. Static analysis; no live execution in this round.

claims.Finding: If a transient attraction owner exists, steers the projectile toward ship center, adjusts speed and then clears owner+160 before calling base motion/lifetime update.
claims.Limitations: Attraction requests must be refreshed by a valid live owner each frame; retaining an old ship pointer is unsafe. Static analysis; no live execution in this round.

claims.Finding: Tests spatial compatibility and projectile collision against companions/main ship, calls1FF340 with the shot's attack descriptor on a main-ship hit, and sets handled-hit byte168. Attraction changes companion handling and nearby visual fading.
claims.Limitations: The read and callback chain is unsuitable for a direct trainer collision call; it assumes valid geometry, companions and effect buffers. Static analysis; no live execution in this round.

claims.Finding: On first projectile update initializes the main sprite control DWORD at its permanent index and configures the effect coordinate mode.
claims.Limitations: The buffer and effect handle must already exist. Static analysis; no live execution in this round.

claims.Finding: Updates main or impact sprite position. During terminal collision it marks the projectile for removal when its impact record is missing or expired; near normal lifetime expiry it scales the main sprite control byte.
claims.Limitations: Impact visual lifetime is separate from main-sprite cleanup. Static analysis; no live execution in this round.

claims.Finding: On collision first clears the main sprite; if handled-hit byte168 is clear, allocates the first free impact sprite index0..127 and reduces projectile speed to30percent.
claims.Limitations: When all128 impact records are busy it returns without allocating one. Native clear does not call this effect-producing path. Static analysis; no live execution in this round.

claims.Finding: Creates the projectile subsystem task on the current Gummi scheduler with group1, priority22000, callback1F6080 and cleanup1F60D0, then initializes ENEMY_SHOT and other projectile families.
claims.Limitations: The task is the useful live-owner witness because the pool globals remain stale after cleanup. Static analysis; no live execution in this round.

claims.Finding: The registered projectile task updates each native projectile family, including ENEMY_SHOT21E970.
claims.Limitations: Presence must be checked in the current scheduler, not inferred from an old task address. Static analysis; no live execution in this round.

claims.Finding: The projectile task cleanup calls ENEMY_SHOT21E8F0 and other projectile-family destructors.
claims.Limitations: No borrowed pool pointer remains valid after this cleanup. Static analysis; no live execution in this round.

claims.Finding: A broader native all-projectile clear calls ENEMY_SHOT21E830 plus four other families.
claims.Limitations: Only ENEMY_SHOT's exact cleanup is fully proposed for trainer use in this round; do not substitute this broader wrapper. Static analysis; no live execution in this round.

claims.Finding: The native radius-clear wrapper calls ENEMY_SHOT21E740 plus four other family radius operations.
claims.Limitations: Those additional families and coordinate contracts need separate verification before exposure. Static analysis; no live execution in this round.

claims.Finding: For each active ENEMY_SHOT obtains world position through23DDD0 and deactivates shots with distanceSquared strictly less than radiusSquared.
claims.Limitations: A radius action would also require reliable world-coordinate input and is not part of the initial two-slot proposal. Static analysis; no live execution in this round.

claims.Finding: The inline32-byte DRAIN object initializes owner0, phase0, counter0, level-1 and warmup0; it has a native vtable.
claims.Limitations: This inline instance belongs to its player and must never be individually freed. Static analysis; no live execution in this round.

claims.Finding: DRAIN's nondestructive destructor only restores its vtable. Player destruction invokes it on the inline object.
claims.Limitations: It is not a safe reset or recreation API. Static analysis; no live execution in this round.

claims.Finding: Installation sets DRAIN phase1 and its owning GUMISHIP pointer.
claims.Limitations: The normal caller first establishes installed Drain parts and their backlinks. Static analysis; no live execution in this round.

claims.Finding: Traverses the main ship part list and attaches the inline DRAIN pointer to every part whose kind is10; returns whether any such part was found.
claims.Limitations: The native traversal assumes a valid, finite packed-pointer list. Raw phase changes do not create these parts. Static analysis; no live execution in this round.

claims.Finding: Recognizes Drain parts by DWORD(part+1224)==10.
claims.Limitations: Part type alone does not prove object ownership or sufficient memory. Static analysis; no live execution in this round.

claims.Finding: Stores the attached DRAIN pointer in DrainPart+1400.
claims.Limitations: This is a borrowed owner link with player/part lifetime dependence. Static analysis; no live execution in this round.

claims.Finding: Player construction creates the inline DRAIN at+4944 and installs it only when main-ship part attachment succeeds; owner is the inline main ship atplayer+1160.
claims.Limitations: A ship without the required installed part remains phase0; forcing phase1 would bypass resource ownership. Static analysis; no live execution in this round.

claims.Finding: Player cleanup clears current-player globalAF0540, destroys inline DRAIN and other player components, and releases effects.
claims.Limitations: No trainer lease should migrate across this destruction or a new player allocation. Static analysis; no live execution in this round.

claims.Finding: Creates a Drain part with kind10 and three guns for attack parameter IDs20/21/22 and projectile types80/81/82, storing them at1376/1384/1392; owner and effect links startnull.
claims.Limitations: Creation allocates and binds native resources and is not proposed as a trainer shortcut. Static analysis; no live execution in this round.

claims.Finding: Drain-part destruction deletes its three guns, clears their pointers, destroys its effect, calls base cleanup and frees the part through the Gummi allocator.
claims.Limitations: Inline DRAIN and part resources have distinct owners. Static analysis; no live execution in this round.

claims.Finding: Drain-part update follows its DRAIN owner, creates the charge effect only while absorbing with a nonnegative charge level, and scales the effect from the native charge fraction.
claims.Limitations: The effect path assumes current effect-resource availability; manipulating its pointer is not proposed. Static analysis; no live execution in this round.

claims.Finding: An equivalent single-argument Drain-part update consumes the same owner/level/fraction fields and updates the attached charge effect.
claims.Limitations: No broader callable ABI is inferred beyond this observed function body. Static analysis; no live execution in this round.

claims.Finding: Drain-part release cancels its charge effect and, for charge level other than-1, requests the gun selected by level at1376+8*level.
claims.Limitations: Level must remain-1..2; values outside that interval can index beyond the three owned guns. Static analysis; no live execution in this round.

claims.Finding: Traverses the main ship's parts and invokes the Drain-part release helper for every kind10 part.
claims.Limitations: Native firing requires a valid current part list and gun/resource ownership. Static analysis; no live execution in this round.

claims.Finding: DRAIN phases are2 warmup,3 reset and enter absorption,4 attract/count/level-up,5 release and6 return to ready1. Warmup threshold is30ticks. Stage thresholds10/30/100 give140 total required absorbed hits for full charge, with at most one level transition per update.
claims.Limitations: Phase0 means uninstalled. Existing broad phase summary is extended here with owner, projectile and exact threshold semantics; no standalone phase patch is proposed. Static analysis; no live execution in this round.

claims.Finding: While phase4, awards native absorption points through233980 and then increments the stage counter only below full level2.
claims.Limitations: Repeated fake absorption calls would change score/progression outcomes, not merely a visual meter. Static analysis; no live execution in this round.

claims.Finding: Awards100 points per absorption, or1000 when current medal value equals30, through the existing score adder207A50.
claims.Limitations: Score-lock behavior is inherited from207A50. The clear-enemy-bullets path does not call this function. Static analysis; no live execution in this round.

claims.Finding: Returns full fraction1 at level2; below that, sums completed thresholds and current stage count then divides by140.
claims.Limitations: The result is not explicitly clamped. A post-projectile/pre-next-stage observation can transiently exceed the nominal progress threshold. Static analysis; no live execution in this round.

claims.Finding: Returns the raw charge-level DWORD, includingFFFFFFFF for level-1.
claims.Limitations: Readouts should interpret it as signed level-1..2, not a huge unsigned level. Static analysis; no live execution in this round.

claims.Finding: Returns whether DRAIN phase equals4 (actively absorbing).
claims.Limitations: A true result does not establish general damage immunity. Static analysis; no live execution in this round.

claims.Finding: Returns whether the DRAIN phase is nonzero (installed/active state family).
claims.Limitations: This includes several nonabsorbing phases. Static analysis; no live execution in this round.

claims.Finding: Returns whether DRAIN phase equals1 (ready).
claims.Limitations: It does not check input or part-resource validity. Static analysis; no live execution in this round.

claims.Finding: Native charge request only changes phase1 to2.
claims.Limitations: Normal input logic can later release the charge; this alone is not a persistent shield control. Static analysis; no live execution in this round.

claims.Finding: Native release request changes phase4 to5; from any other phase it resets phase1, count0, warmup0 and level-1.
claims.Limitations: Calling outside the normal ready/absorption flow can cancel a warmup rather than fire. Static analysis; no live execution in this round.

claims.Finding: Unconditionally resets DRAIN to ready1 with count0, level-1 and warmup0; current xref query found no callers.
claims.Limitations: Unreferenced helper semantics do not justify exposing it as the normal gameplay API. Static analysis; no live execution in this round.

claims.Finding: Resets DRAIN counters and directly enters absorption phase4; current xref query found no callers.
claims.Limitations: This skips warmup and does not prove correct input/effect ownership, so it remains research only. Static analysis; no live execution in this round.

claims.Finding: One native input mode starts/releases DRAIN according to inputbit0x100 combined with configuration9BA860bit0, and manages the player-side absorption effect.
claims.Limitations: Physical button mapping is not inferred; a one-shot start may be undone by normal input on later frames. Static analysis; no live execution in this round.

claims.Finding: The alternate input path applies the same DRAIN input/configuration logic while also handling movement/roll controls.
claims.Limitations: No synthetic held-input override has been verified or proposed. Static analysis; no live execution in this round.

claims.Finding: Only attack descriptor kind1 is absorbed while DRAIN is installed and phase4; it calls231350 and returns before HP damage. Other attacks follow the normal ship damage path.
claims.Limitations: This is projectile-kind-specific absorption, not universal invulnerability. Static analysis; no live execution in this round.

claims.Finding: The integer ship-damage path has no DRAIN absorption check and proceeds through its own flags/HP handling.
claims.Limitations: A DRAIN phase control would not protect against all damage entrypoints. Static analysis; no live execution in this round.

claims.Finding: At maximum charge, schedules the special fiber231CA0 on the Gummi scheduler (group1,priority22100) and installs cleanup231D00 under a shared busy flag.
claims.Limitations: This has asynchronous effects and broader projectile clears; it is not the proposed direct clear API. Static analysis; no live execution in this round.

claims.Finding: The maximum-charge special sequence performs native visual transitions and waits, calls broad projectile clear1F6050, waits again, then ends its task.
claims.Limitations: Timing and other projectile families are engine-owned; no manual fiber invocation is proposed. Static analysis; no live execution in this round.

claims.Finding: Another native special sequence uses the shared busy flag, visual transition/wait, broad clear1F6050 and further gameplay operations.
claims.Limitations: This corroborates legitimate in-mission clearing but does not make all its side effects safe to generalize. Static analysis; no live execution in this round.

claims.Finding: Another native special sequence performs fades/waits and broad projectile clear1F6050 before its own follow-up operation.
claims.Limitations: No universal enemy-kill or mission-win interpretation is made. Static analysis; no live execution in this round.

claims.Finding: Special-sequence cleanup clears the shared busy flagAF95E0.
claims.Limitations: Do not clear this flag independently while an engine-owned fiber is active. Static analysis; no live execution in this round.

claims.Finding: Allocates a152-byte task, stores callback+0, manager+88, group+96, priority+100, cleanup+104 and fiber+112, then inserts it in the manager head16/tail24 doubly linked list using next120/previous128 in ascending priority order.
claims.Limitations: Allocation and list insertion are engine operations; trainer code only validates the current list. Static analysis; no live execution in this round.

claims.Finding: Unlinks a task and zeroes its next/previous links before invoking cleanup+104, then frees the task and optional fiber through its owning manager.
claims.Limitations: This ordering makes the current linked task a useful ENEMY_SHOT lifetime witness; a cached task address is insufficient. Static analysis; no live execution in this round.

claims.Finding: Manager destruction traverses linked tasks, unlinks each before cleanup, destroys optional fibers, frees tasks and finally frees the manager.
claims.Limitations: The Gummi module scheduler and heap identity still must be validated before reading the list. Static analysis; no live execution in this round.

claims.Finding: Scheduler dispatch sets manager+32 to the current task, invokes direct callbacks or fibers, then clears+32 and retires callbacks that became null.
claims.Limitations: The proposed trainer clear requires manager+32==0 and executes after the native outer update on the game thread. Static analysis; no live execution in this round.

claims.Finding: Gummi allocation delegates to virtual slot+8 on heap globalAE94F0, matching the allocation path used by the ENEMY_SHOT pool initializer.
claims.Limitations: A raw readable pointer alone is not a proof of a live allocation. Static analysis; no live execution in this round.

claims.Finding: Gummi free delegates to virtual slot+16 on the same heap globalAE94F0.
claims.Limitations: Pool pointers must not be reused across heap or module replacement. Static analysis; no live execution in this round.

claims.Finding: Main-ship collision refreshes native geometry and tests its two indexed geometry arrays against an incoming shape, returning after the first collision.
claims.Limitations: This read/update path assumes valid native geometry counts and arrays; it is not a proposed trainer call. Static analysis; no live execution in this round.

claims.Finding: Special ship-part collision selects only part IDs599/600, supplies radii20/30 in XMM2 to the shape builder and tests them against the incoming shape.
claims.Limitations: Other part IDs contribute no positive radius in this path. No claim of general shield invulnerability is made. Static analysis; no live execution in this round.
